content: Polysorbate 20, also commercially known as Tween 20, is a surfactant belonging to the polysorbate family. Its chemical stability and relatively low toxicity make it suitable for use as a detergent and emulsifier in various domestic, scientific, and pharmacological applications. Chemically, it is a polyoxyethylene derivative of sorbitan monolaurate. It is differentiated from other members of the Tween series by the length of its polyoxyethylene chain and the specific fatty acid ester moiety it contains. The commercial product is not a single compound but rather a mixture of chemical species. Food Applications Tween 20 is utilized as a wetting agent in flavored mouth drops, such as Ice Drops. It enhances the spreading sensation of other ingredients, including SD alcohol and mint flavor. The World Health Organization (WHO) has established acceptable daily intake limits for polyoxyethylene sorbitan esters, recommending a range of 0–25 mg per kilogram of body weight. Biological Applications In the biological sciences, Tween 20 has a wide array of uses. For instance: It is employed to stabilize purified protein derivative (PPD) solutions, which are used in skin testing for tuberculosis exposure. It serves as a blocking agent in immunoassays, such as Western blots and ELISAs, where it is often used at a concentration of 0.05% v/v. Additionally, it is incorporated into washing solutions for immunoassays to reduce nonspecific binding. Pharmaceutical Applications In pharmaceutical formulations, Tween 20 is used to stabilize emulsions and suspensions, ensuring the uniform distribution of active ingredients. Industrial and Domestic Applications Tween 20 is also found in industrial and domestic cleaning products. For example, it is listed as a key ingredient in the cleaning solution manufactured by Clorox for use in the iRobot Scooba floor-washing robot, as indicated in its Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS).
